City council approves new transit budget

The city council voted 7-2 on Tuesday to approve a transit budget that expands bus service across the northern districts and adds two new express routes by next spring.

Supporters said the plan would cut commute times for thousands of residents, while critics argued the council had not explained how the operating costs would be covered after the first three years. The mayor is expected to sign the measure later this week.

"This is a long overdue investment in the people who keep this city running," said the council president during the hearing, which lasted nearly four hours and drew dozens of public comments.

The transit authority will publish a detailed schedule for the new routes in the coming months.
